tagline: Along the mountain rim, above the old lumber roads.
intro: From Cajon Pass, the byway follows the rim of the San Bernardino Mountains toward San Gorgonio Pass, using Highways 138, 18 and 38. Near Crestline, Lake Gregory occupies the old Houston Flat; farther along, Running Springs stands above six thousand feet.

In the years around 1900 a logging railroad near Running Springs worked the high country with no link to the lines below, so its Shay locomotives were taken apart and hauled up the mountain by wagon. The locomotives made the climb as freight.

moments.title: Lake Gregory
moments.text: At Crestline, a reservoir expected to take three years to fill did the job in three days during the rains of 1938.

moments.title: Running Springs
moments.text: From the old Fredalba mill near Running Springs, most of the lumber went down the steep grades by wagon to a Highland factory making citrus crates.

moments.title: Angelus Oaks
moments.text: The lodge at Angelus Oaks began as a stagecoach stop where horses were changed and passengers were served sandwiches.

practical: The byway is open year-round, but winter snow can require tire chains.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Rim of the World Scenic Byway
